newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay to lead roadshow on Thai Yankee bond.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay to lead roadshow on Thai Yankee bond.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday he would lead a roadshow for a planned $500 million Thai Yankee bond in Hong Kong early next week amid concern that Moody's Investors Service is reviewing the country's sovereign debts.
Amnuay told reporters Thailand would provide Moody's and Standard and Poor's with updated information on its economy but said the two rating agencies had discretion on whether to downgrade Thailand.
Asked about the impact of Moody's possible downgrade of Thailand, Amnuay said: "Under the current circumstances, it would not augur well for Thailand."
The minister said Moody's would send economists to survey the Thai economy early next month after it based its earlier decision on information gathered mainly from the media.
Moody's said on Friday it might cut Thailand's A2 long-term foreign currency debt and deposit ratings.
It said the review was prompted by concerns over the soundness of Thailand's financial sector, as well as by constraints on macroeconomic policy-making.
Standard and Poor's, however, said on Friday it had no plans to downgrade Thailand, reiterating its view that the sovereign was strong enough to weather problems in the banking sector.
Amnuay said all government agencies have been instructed to prepare updated information for presentation to the Moody's team which, he said, is expected to spend a few months on its Thai survey.
He said he would brief fund managers in Hong Kong on Monday on the Thai economy's current fundamentals.
